answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed identity. Before an agent can transact, it must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers prove duplicate or fraudulent behaviour. An onyx registry records each stake, so creating many fake agents multiplies the capital at risk rather than giving free influence. An atlas of reputation links past work to the same stake, so a fresh identity starts worthless. Like a falcon that must prove itself before joining the flock, an agent earns trust only through costly, verifiable participation, forcing a Sybil attacker to pay for every copy and lose it when caught.
